messages:
Anna (ML): Hey team — kicking off onboarding for `starling-14b` (fp16 checkpoint we got from model-onboarding). Need a perf baseline + quantization experiments so we can recommend a production config. Looking for a concise bench plan: throughput/latency, batching profiles, context-length sweeps, and what GPU/slot shapes to try. Priority: customer POC next week. @Mario @Lucy
Mario: I can own the perf harness. Proposed minimal plan: 1) baseline fp16, 2) q4_1, 3) q4_0 with KV quant enabled/disabled. Targets: 8k context nominal, priming seq=1024, generation window=256 tokens. Batch sizes: [1,2,4,8,16]. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 lat, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory headroom, OOMs. I'll collect kernel traces.
Mario: Using perf-runner; example command: 
```bash
perf-runner --model starling-14b --mode generation --ctx 8192 --prompt-len 1024 --gen-tokens 256 --batches 1,2,4,8,16 --quant fp16 --out-dir gs://redwood-perf/starling-14b/baseline
```
Mario: Will also run synthetic and real prompts. Synthetic for throughput, real for tail latency + eval hooks.
Lucy Chen: For quality/regression: run the 1k prompt eval suite (evals/regression-set-2025-v2). Report avg logprob delta vs fp16 baseline, and automated hallucination checks (entity hallucination FPR). For q4 configs include token-level logprob diffs and a small manual spot-check (10 prompts) for instruction-following.
Lucy Chen: Quant notes — q4_1 usually preserves more fp32 headroom than q4_0, but q4_0 sometimes gives better memory savings. With KV cache quant we might see >2x memory reduction but watch perf regressions for long ctx. Add this to hypothesis sheet.
Ben Patel: Quick infra note — staging has A10G and a limited H100 pool. H100 is ~2x speed for 14B in our kernels but we only have 4 GPUs available in staging right now. If you need larger concurrency tests, request Dedicated capacity (I can reserve 2 H100 for 2h).
deploy-bot: perf-job starling-14b-baseline started by Mario — job id `pj-2025-0893` — logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/perf/pj-2025-0893
Anna (ML): Thanks. Deliverables: 1) perf report with plots (latency CDFs, tokens/sec vs batch), 2) CSVs for raw traces, 3) recommended production config (GPU type, batch sizing, quantization setting, cache policy), 4) short QA note on quality regressions and acceptance criteria. Timeline: baseline by EOD Wed, quant runs Thu, writeup Fri morning.
Mario: Plan accepted. I'll capture kernel-selection logs with `--trace-kernels` and include a short appendix showing which kernels were chosen for each ctx/batch. Also will run continuous-batching stress for 30m to surface tail behavior.
Lucy Chen: Add context-length sweep: 512, 2048, 4096, 8192. For each ctx, record peak GPU memory and perf curves. Also include warm vs cold cache runs (3 reps each). Use eval harness config: 
```json
{"model":"starling-14b","quant_modes":["fp16","q4_1","q4_0_kv"],"ctx_lengths":[512,2048,4096,8192],"batches":[1,2,4,8,16]}
```
(We'll paste this into the perf job UI)
Ben Patel: Reminder: when you open the Dedicated reservation ticket, include expected GPU hours and concurrency targets. I can attach cost estimate. For the POC, H100 + q4_1 looks like the sweet spot if quality holds.
Anna (ML): Acceptance criteria suggestion: no more than 5% drop in avg logprob vs fp16 for top-1 generation; latency p95 under 300ms at batch=1 on H100 for 256-token outputs. If q4_1 meets cost goals and passes eval, default to it.
Mario: Noted. I'll post interim plots to the perf channel and upload raw CSVs to gs://redwood-perf/starling-14b/results/1747203845/
Lucy Chen: I'll schedule the 1k eval run after Mario's fp16 baseline completes so we have a clean comparator.
Anna (ML): Cool. Small checklist for the run owner (Mario):
- verify checkpoint checksum + config (model-card)
- run fp16 baseline (A10G + H100 if possible)
- run quant variants q4_1, q4_0_kv (same seeds where applicable)
- ctx sweep + batch sweep (store p50/p95/p99)
- continuous-batching stress 30m (monitor tail)
- attach kernel traces and memory logs
- run 1k eval suite and produce logprob diffs
- produce final recommendation + cost delta table

Mario: Got it. I'll create a Google doc and link it here when the baseline completes.
Anna (ML): Thanks all — ping me if any blockers. :thumbsup:
